body.statement: For every admissible \((h,k,J_\pi,J_\mu)\), the released set \(C_n(h,k)\) is replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private and satisfies \(\inf_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}\Pr_Q\{\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\in C_n(h,k)\}\ge1-\eta\). Coverage probability integrates the sampling law, all pilot and moment Gaussian noises, and the deterministic sample split.
body.justification: The headline converts a fully privatized higher-order CATE learner into an honest pointwise causal interval.
body.gap: SchroederHartensteinFeuerriegel2025 proves a private interval for the regular population ATE, while no located theorem gives uniform pointwise Hölder CATE coverage with higher-order nuisance bias.
body.consumer: A hospital can release a confidence interval for the treatment effect at a prespecified clinical profile while protecting every patient record.

obligation.what_is_open: Deduce unconditional honest coverage and privacy after proving the two load-bearing release and remainder lemmas.
obligation.obstruction: The theorem depends essentially on both unresolved lemmas; treating their conclusions as assumptions would assume the crux.
obligation.attempted: The deterministic coverage reduction from identification and the radius definition is complete, but the probability and privacy premises are unavailable.
obligation.partial_result: Conditional on the two unresolved lemmas, the result is immediate: the remainder event has probability at least \(1-\eta\), pointwise identification replaces \(\tau_Q(x_0)\) by \(\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\), and the definition of \(C_n(h,k)\) then gives coverage; privacy follows from the release lemma and post-processing.  Since both load-bearing premises remain unproved from the current learner definition, this conditional reduction does not establish the theorem.
